title: Halloween
full_review:
One of the strong points of John Carpenter�s 1978 cult horror film �Halloween,� was its subtlety. The film suggested, more than showed, the menace posed by its psychotic villain, Michael Myers. It also managed to generate a maximum of suspense and fear with a minimum of gore, by today�s standards (For the record, the Catholic Film Office still deemed it an �O.�)

That ratio is precisely and fatally reversed in writer-director Rob Zombie�s remake. This �Halloween� (Dimension) is egregiously sadistic, wallowing in blood, gore, screams and the dying desperation of its victims, some of whom can be seen crawling across floors or staggering down hallways in an effort to escape their inevitable fate.

Indeed the killing sprees of both the young Michael Myers (Daeg Faerch) and his hulking adult incarnation (Tyler Mane) begin to take on a routine feel that undercuts any real suspense.

Whether it�s Michael the boy murdering Ronnie (William Forsythe), his stripper mother�s (Sheri Moon Zombie) deadbeat boyfriend and then dispatching his wayward older sister, Judith (Hanna Hall) or whether it�s the long incarcerated adult, breaking out of the sanitarium to terrorize his pompous psychiatrist, Dr. Samuel Loomis (Malcolm McDowell, who should know better) and his younger sister, Laurie (Scout Taylor Compton), the whole proceeding is just another day at the slaughter house.

In place of the level headed, resourceful and determined heroine of the earlier version, played by Jamie Lee Curtis, we are now confronted with a victim who can barely figure out how to dial 911. What was once a plausible struggle between two well matched adversaries, one a killing machine and the other a feisty survivor, has now become a relentless hunt for hapless prey.

The French have a saying: �It�s worse than a crime, it�s a mistake.� This latest �Halloween,� however, manages to be both those things at once.

The film contains scenes of prolonged, gruesome and bloody violence with gore, sexual activity, rear and upper female nudity, obscene gestures, pervasive rough, crude and crass language, and scatological humor.
